definitions.meaning: a sign of the zodiac, the eighth one, symbolised by the stinging arachnid

explanation.walkthrough: 'of an' is just a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the zodiac sign and the British light reconnaissance tank carry this name.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the piece is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: the on side is the leg side in cricket, so legs can be ONS

explanation.surface: Someone takes a tumble and ends up sprawled with legs in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the cricket piece round (SNO). In cricket the leg side of the pitch is also called the on side, so legs can be ONS.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall of the white winter stuff, as in 'a heavy fall overnight', is a synonym for the precipitation itself.

indicators.note: a translation turns words into new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive is ignored and the letters ONES are used

explanation.surface: A remark that the translated version of the first chapter reads oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' rearranges the letters into OSEN. In the King James Bible the Israelites are 'a peculiar people', meaning set apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical sense of peculiar is specially selected or set apart, as God's own people.

parts.note: states are countries or nations

explanation.surface: A note about territories located within European nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Landed properties, the grounds of a country house, are synonyms for the plural noun.

parts.note: the calendar date changes, or moves on, at the stroke of twelve at night; the surface suggests a romantic or emotional date

explanation.definitionFit: Twelve o'clock at night is the moment when one calendar day rolls over to the next.

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
neck is British slang for cheek or audacity

explanation.surface: A robbery is shown to require nerve and cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold-up' suggests a robbery, but here it means a traffic jam or delay. 'shows' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow point that causes congestion and delay is a synonym for a hold-up in traffic or production.

definitions.meaning: to back a motion or proposal formally

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means a very short moment, and the verb means to back a proposal at a meeting.

indicators.note: producing suggests something new is made out of the letters, so they are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A suntan so good that it seems to have been grown by a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producing' is the signal to rearrange SUCHATAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Bear's breech is a Mediterranean flowering plant whose leaves inspired Corinthian capitals.

indicators.note: after places the two men following the one in the answer

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Ron is a man's name
Ed is another man's name

explanation.surface: Two men move in after a single person has occupied an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment, but it is the adjective: pressed smooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that have been pressed are smoothed out, so flattened, the adjectival sense.

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for custody backwards

parts.note: ward means custody or guardianship, as in 'in ward'

explanation.surface: Someone trying to regain custody of a child.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something, as in drawing water or a salary, is a synonym for getting it.

indicators.note: surprisingly hints the letters turn up in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A comment that, oddly, someone is not opposed to doing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of no movement or development is a synonym for inertia.

clue.text: Jack returns to Rock for monkey

parts.note: the Rock is Gibraltar, often shortened to Gib

indicators.note: returns says the word for jack is turned round

parts.note: in cribbage the jack is called his nob

explanation.surface: A sailor named Jack goes back to Gibraltar to fetch a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns the cribbage word round (BON). Gibraltar is famous for its Barbary apes, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-armed ape is loosely a monkey in everyday speech.

indicators.note: compiling suggests the letters are assembled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone named Beth loves setting crosswords like this one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compiling' rearranges BETHADORES. 'this' points at the large-format newspaper in which the puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: The puzzle was printed in a large-format quality newspaper, so 'this' points to that kind of paper.

parts.note: Egg was a well-known British online bank
heads for means aims for or goes towards

explanation.surface: An online bank targets academics as customers.
explanation.walkthrough: Egg was a UK internet bank launched in the late 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Intellectuals or bookish people are informally called by this term.

indicators.note: battered suggests something knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boxing champion with a bruised red nose.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause is to support or back it publicly, a synonym verb.

clue.text: An aperient upset a Queen's meal

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the piece is turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: Queen Anne is a British monarch, giving Anne's
tea is an afternoon or evening meal

explanation.surface: A laxative spoiled a queen's dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: An infusion of senna leaves is a traditional laxative, which is what an aperient is.

parts.note: roads are a kind of thoroughfare, and the idiom for being far in front uses the plural word for urban roads

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'X ahead' means far in advance, and X is also a plural of town roads.

clue.text: Drone away in your old, sad song

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the old word for your

parts.note: thy is the old form of your

indicators.note: away suggests the letters wander off into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The drone of the bagpipes in an old lament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' rearranges the insect word into RENOD, which 'in' puts inside the archaic possessive; 'old' marks that form as dated.
explanation.definitionFit: A song of lamentation for the dead is a dirge, a sad song.

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the word for mower

parts.note: a cutter is something that mows, a mower

explanation.surface: Garden rubbish left in the lawnmower.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess of untidy things lying about is a synonym for litter.
The adjective means chief or principal, and the noun is a deep red like a churchman's robes.

parts.note: mused means thought or pondered

explanation.surface: Someone who held an idea in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertained a thought' reads as considering an idea; it splits as definition plus A plus MUSED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be diverted or made to smile is a synonym for being entertained.

clue.text: Janet and Josephine were two makers of bloomers

definitions.meaning: Dame Janet Baker the mezzo-soprano and Josephine Baker the entertainer shared a surname
a bloomer is a British loaf of bread, so its makers work in a bakery

explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' suggests underwear, but a bloomer is a crusty loaf in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The two famous women shared this surname, and bread-makers bake bloomer loaves.

indicators.note: in recital means as spoken out, so the word is heard

parts.note: a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A poet banned from giving a reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Prohibited or excluded is a synonym for forbidden.

indicators.note: ornamental suggests the letters are decoratively rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A decorative garden bush subdues a serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: A large venomous pit viper of Central and South America goes by this name.
The word names a Chinese sailing ship, discarded rubbish, and slang for the drug.

clue.text: He's still dear to his jilter

definitions.text: He's still dear to his jilter

parts.words: He's still dear to his jilter
parts.note: a break-up letter traditionally opens with the salutation 'Dear' and the man's name, so the jilted man is still addressed as dear

explanation.definitionFit: The classic break-up letter to a man is addressed 'Dear' plus this common man's name.

clue.text: Where vessel in reverse shows stern

indicators.note: reverse says the run found there is read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words Where vessel, across the word break

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Where on a ship the stern is shown, as when a vessel goes astern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the run concealed across 'Where vessel'; 'reverse' turns EREVES round. 'shows' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern meaning strict or harsh is a synonym for severe; 'shows' is a link.

clue.text: Kind of sun block applied to forehead

definitions.text: Kind of sun block applied to forehead

parts.words: Kind of sun block applied to forehead
parts.note: not a lotion but a visor worn on the brow that shades the eyes from sunlight

explanation.definitionFit: A visor worn on the forehead to shield the eyes from glare blocks the sun.
